transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Yeah, so… the main thing is I feel like I keep hitting this wall with work that needs real sitting-down brain effort. Like monthly reports, or when I have to plan something across multiple sites, a health event or whatever—it matters, I know it matters, but I’ll keep putting it off.

And it’s not that I don’t care. I manage health services, so there’s always some moving part, and I can handle a lot of quick issues as they come up. But when it’s something where I have to sit, focus, organize my thoughts, and really grind through it, I just sort of… avoid it. Then I end up stressed because it’s still there.
Do you find that your mind tends to wander or that you get easily distracted, especially when you’re trying to focus on tasks that require sustained attention?

Yeah, definitely. Like in meetings, if I’m trying to follow a budget update, I’ll be listening and then someone’s phone vibrates, or there’s people talking out in the hallway, and suddenly I’m gone from the conversation.

Or even it’ll be something inside my own head, like I’ll remember something I forgot to do for the league I help with, and then I’m thinking about that for a minute, and by the time I come back I’ve missed the next few minutes of what was being said. Then I’m sitting there trying to piece it together like, okay, where are we now?
Have you noticed yourself feeling down, sad, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy, especially around the time you’re avoiding these tasks?

I don’t know that I’d call it sad, exactly. I mean, I get frustrated with myself, sure, because the task is still sitting there and I know I’m making it worse by putting it off.

But losing interest in things… I’m not sure. Like, I still enjoy the usual stuff when I actually get to it. Sometimes I’ll get caught up thinking about work when I’m supposed to be doing something else, like last weekend I was at my nephew’s game and I kept remembering this spreadsheet I hadn’t finished—sorry, that’s probably not what you’re asking.

So… no, I haven’t really noticed feeling down in that way. More stressed and annoyed with myself than sad.
Have you been feeling more tired or lacking energy lately, even when you’re not doing anything particularly taxing?

I’m not sure, honestly. I mean, I get tired like anybody does, but I haven’t really noticed some big change where I’m wiped out for no reason.

Sometimes after work I’ll feel drained, but then work is… you know, there’s always something. Yesterday I went in just to handle one issue and ended up talking to three different people about scheduling and then someone needed a form fixed—sorry, that’s not really about energy.

So, no, I don’t think I’d say I’m unusually tired lately. More like mentally worn out when I’ve been dealing with a lot.
Do you often feel restless or find it hard to relax, even when you have some downtime?

Hmm… restless, like physically? I don’t know, not really in a way I’ve paid attention to.

I mean, if I have downtime I usually can sit and watch a game or something, though sometimes I’ll start thinking about, you know, whether I replied to somebody or if there’s something I was supposed to do. But that’s not exactly “restless,” I guess.

Actually, last night I had the TV on and I kept checking the score of another game on my phone, and then I remembered I needed to—sorry, I’m getting off track. I don’t think I’d say I’m especially restless or unable to relax. Not that I’ve noticed.
Outside of work, do you find yourself forgetting things, losing track of where you put items, or having trouble staying organized in your daily routine?

Yeah… outside of work it does happen. I don’t know if I’d say I’m totally disorganized, but I do forget things more than I’d like.

Like with some community events I help with, I’ll forget to return calls from volunteers, or I’ll say I’m going to pick up some small errand item and then it just falls out of my head. And there’ve been one or two times where a meeting completely slipped my mind until someone texted me, and then I’m rushing around apologizing.

It’s embarrassing, honestly, because these aren’t huge complicated things. It’s more like little routine stuff just doesn’t stay where I put it in my brain.
Looking back, were you someone who had trouble staying focused or tended to forget things often even when you were younger, like in school or when you had responsibilities at home?

Yeah, I guess that does go back pretty far. In elementary school, I remember teachers telling my parents I was bright, but that I was always kind of… off in my own world. Daydreaming a lot.

And I’d lose worksheets all the time, or forget to turn in homework. My mom used to check my backpack every night because otherwise something would just sit in there crumpled up, even if I’d actually done it.

It’s funny, I can still picture those old folders—well, not funny exactly, more like embarrassing. But yeah, it wasn’t just an adult thing.
Have these issues with focus and forgetfulness ever significantly affected your relationships, social life, or other important areas of your life outside of work?

Yeah… I mean, I’m still getting by. It’s not like my life has fallen apart or anything. I show up, I do the things I’m supposed to do most of the time.

But outside of work—and honestly sometimes around work people too—there have been times where somebody else had to kind of cover the gap because I dropped the ball. Like I missed a deadline or forgot to follow up, and then I’m doing that whole last-minute apology thing. I hate that. I’ve had to text friends or coworkers like, “I’m so sorry, I completely meant to get back to you,” which sounds flimsy after a while.

And then I worry people think I don’t care, which isn’t true. Like with friends, if I forget to respond or forget something we talked about, it can come across badly. I don’t think it’s destroyed relationships, but it has definitely caused embarrassment and some strain here and there.
Do these issues with focus and forgetfulness happen in different parts of your life, like at home or in social situations, or are they mostly limited to when you're at work?

It’s not just work, no. I mean, work is where it shows up more obviously because there are deadlines and people notice when something doesn’t get done.

But it happens at home and with community stuff too. Like I’ll be doing okay overall, I’m not falling apart or anything, but then I’ll forget to follow up with someone, or something slips and somebody else has to kind of patch it over for me. And then I’m stuck doing that awkward, “I’m so sorry, I meant to handle that,” message.

Actually, that happened with a friend recently—well, not recently exactly, I don’t know, time gets weird—but it was one of those things where I forgot to respond and then by the time I remembered, it felt worse to answer late. So yeah, it’s in different parts of my life, not only at work.

Do you also find yourself struggling with focus or forgetfulness in more personal aspects of your life, like taking care of daily routines such as showering, eating regularly, or keeping up with chores around the house?

Yeah, some of that spills over into personal life too. I mean, with showering or eating, I don’t know if that’s the main thing I’d point to, but chores and little responsibilities, definitely.

Like with community event stuff—I’ve forgotten to return calls from volunteers, or I’ll mean to run some small errand for an event and then it just… disappears from my head. And once or twice I’ve had to apologize because a community meeting completely slipped my mind until someone texted me, like, “Are you still coming?” Which is a terrible feeling.

It’s weird because I can be thinking about the thing earlier in the day, and then by the time I’m supposed to do it, my brain has moved on to something totally different.
